items.prompt: What is the boundary between a Load Balancer outbound rule and NAT Gateway?
constraints: Outbound rules provide explicit SNAT configuration for Standard Load Balancer backends using a frontend IP and allocated ports.
Size SNAT ports for concurrency and prefer NAT Gateway when its subnet-level model better fits outbound-only scale.

options.text: An outbound rule always overrides every subnet route.
An outbound rule supplies SNAT for members of a Load Balancer backend pool; NAT Gateway supplies scalable subnet-level outbound SNAT independent of inbound load-balancing rules.
NAT Gateway distributes inbound application traffic while outbound rules route subnets.
Both require public IPs on every backend NIC.
